columns.name: task_id
columns.description: Stable task identifier matching task-plan.md. Use the same identifier for every row belonging to one task.

columns.name: group_id
columns.description: Comparison group with the same target metric, protocol and population. Rank only within this group; never compare ranks across groups.

columns.name: candidate_id
columns.description: Stable candidate identifier, identical to the model-visible task plan. Unique within task_id + group_id. Never use spreadsheet row position as the identity.

columns.name: candidate_description
columns.description: Explain the candidate, treatment or condition and all distinguishing parameters. Match the plan and give units for any quantities.

columns.name: metric
columns.description: Outcome being ranked, including assay, endpoint, normalization and measurement time. Keep the definition consistent within a group.

columns.name: unit
columns.description: Unit of the target metric. Write dimensionless for a unitless metric. Use numeric values in observed_value; do not append unit text to numbers.

columns.name: direction
columns.description: higher_first means rank 1 has the highest metric value. lower_first means rank 1 has the lowest. This specifies ordering, not whether an outcome is desirable.

columns.name: rank
columns.description: Reference rank within a group, starting at 1. Use dense ranks, e.g. 1, 2, 2, 3. Equal ranks are evidence-supported ties. Leave blank for unknown or excluded rows; do not use 0.

columns.name: relation_status
columns.description: ranked: the reference relation is supported; unknown: insufficient evidence to rank; excluded: intentionally outside scoring, with a reason in notes. Unknown is not a tie.

columns.name: observed_value
columns.description: Measured or curated reference value used to justify the rank. Explain preprocessing and aggregation in the plan. Leave missing values blank; a real zero remains numeric 0.

columns.name: n_replicates
columns.description: Number of independent replicates supporting the reference value. Distinguish biological/experimental and technical replicates in the plan. Leave blank if unavailable.

columns.name: uncertainty
columns.description: Uncertainty measure, value, units and interval level or replicate range. State whether this is SD, SEM or a confidence interval. If unavailable, explain the limitation in notes.

columns.name: evidence_ref
columns.description: Locatable evidence for the reference answer or unknown/excluded status: file + sheet/cell, figure/table, DOI, sample or experiment identifier. Link raw data rather than only a narrative conclusion.

columns.name: notes
columns.description: Tie justification, missing-data reason, exclusion reason, reviewer decision or other qualifications. Define every additional column in Column guide with its type, unit and allowed values.
columns.example: Tie follows the prespecified tolerance in task-plan.md, section 8.

sections.title: Task identity and scientific objective
sections.detail: Task ID, version, title, discipline, author/contact, scientific question, significance and the exact capability being evaluated.

sections.title: Prediction target and comparison groups
sections.detail: What must be predicted, the target metric and units, measurement time, ranking direction, group boundaries and required output format.

sections.title: Candidate definitions
sections.detail: Every candidate ID, description, structure/composition, treatment, dose and distinguishing parameters. IDs must match the answer workbook exactly.

sections.title: Experimental protocol and conditions
sections.detail: Materials, preparation, instruments and settings, quantities and units, environment, timing, controls, replicates, randomization/blinding and relevant deviations.

sections.title: Information available to the model
sections.detail: The self-contained task prompt, allowed inputs and files, permitted tools/web access, time or compute budget and what must be withheld from the model.

sections.title: Reference data and provenance
sections.detail: Original data source, experiment/sample IDs, collection dates, raw-file locations, measurement methods, preprocessing, normalization, aggregation and data quality checks.

sections.title: Reference ranking and scientific rationale
sections.detail: Explain how the answer workbook was derived, the evidence for each ordering, relevant mechanisms, assumptions and expert adjudication. Keep this out of model-visible inputs. Publication permissions follow the chosen submission channel.

sections.title: Ties, uncertainty and missing comparisons
sections.detail: Prespecified tie criterion/tolerance, precision and uncertainty, missing or excluded candidates, incomplete comparisons and why any pair cannot be ordered. Unknown is not a tie.

sections.title: Scoring and acceptance rules
sections.detail: Submission schema, rank convention, proposed scoring rule, treatment of ties, unknown pairs, missing/duplicate IDs and invalid outputs. Include a worked scoring example.

sections.title: Reproducibility and task packaging
sections.detail: Required files, software/environment versions, seeds, dependencies, estimated runtime and resources, reproduction steps and optional existing Harbor package.

sections.title: Rights, confidentiality and leakage controls
sections.detail: Ownership and permission to share for review, disclosure restrictions, answer/evidence separation, potentially public material and contamination or leakage risks.

sections.title: Limitations and author checklist
sections.detail: Known confounders and failure modes, unresolved questions, checked candidate coverage, complete column definitions, source evidence and consistency between the plan and workbook.
